packageRules.description: The superpom carries the Spring Boot version, so a superpom minor is a Spring Boot minor. org.entur packages are exempt from the shared release-age cooldown, so an automerged bump would land unreviewed the day it is published.

Camel is not SemVer compliant, so a minor may carry breaking changes and must be reviewed and tested on its own. Keep it out of the all-minor-patch aggregate PR and give it a dedicated one; only patch updates stay in the aggregate. Both artifacts share camel.version, so they must be grouped together to avoid conflicting branches. The shared config only guards camel-spring-boot-bom, but camel.version also drives camel-test-spring-junit5.
kubernetes-client must track the version camel-kubernetes pins; a bump ahead of Camel splits the fabric8 stack and only fails at runtime
